newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty condemns massacre in Zaire refugee camp.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty condemns massacre in Zaire refugee camp.

text.p: Up to 500 unarmed Rwandan Hutu refugees and displaced Zaireans have been killed in a massacre by Tutsi rebels at a camp in Zaire, international human rights group Amnesty International said on Tuesday.
It called for an "immediate international presence" to investigate the killings and said those responsible should be brought to justice.

On Monday, local Zaireans showed reporters bodies lying in the Chimanga Camp, 40 kilometres (25 miles) southwest of the regional capital Bukavu. They said 300 Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees had been killed.
"The victims of last week's massacre include Father Jean-Claude Buhendwa, a Zairean Roman Catholic priest of nearby Burhale parish," Amnesty said in a statement.
"These arbitrary and deliberate mass killings of defenceless civilians are a callous abuse of human rights and should be condemned by the international community," it added.

"Governments and organisations which are supporting this armed group should take responsibility to ensure that the perpetrators, including their leaders who ordered these killings, are brought to justice and prevented from carrying out further violations."
Up to 30,000 Hutu refugees lived at Chimanga Camp, but most fled last month after fighting broke out between Tutsi rebels who now control much of Eastern Zaire and the Zairean army.
Amnesty said the armed group, the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL), found the refugees on November 18 and separated men from women.
"AFDL combatants then opened fire on the men, killing all of them," it said.
The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) estimated there were 1.2 million Rwandan refugees in the camps in eastern Zaire until mid-November.

The Rwandan refugees first fled Rwanda in 1994, fearing reprisals from the victorious Rwandan Patriotic Front after a genocide of up to one million Tutsis and moderate Hutus organised by Hutu extremists in the former government.
"Amnesty International is calling for an immediate international presence to investigate the killings and other abuses by the AFDL and others, and to prevent their recurrence."
